Sheri Haugen-Hoffart

Republican candidate for Public Service Commissioner (six-year term), North Dakota · Incumbent

North Dakota Public Service Commissioner (incumbent)

Sheri Haugen-Hoffart is a Republican member of the North Dakota Public Service Commission. Gov. Doug Burgum appointed her in February 2022, and voters elected her to the seat later that year. She won the June 9, 2026 Republican primary for a six-year term with 64% of the vote and faces Democratic-NPL candidate John Pederson on November 3.

Where Haugen-Hoffart stands

Energy affordability / utility rates
Credits the PSC's 'great oversight' for North Dakota's electricity rates being the lowest in the country. Says 'We have good policy right now' and does not see a great need for change.
Coal and natural gas
Says coal and natural gas play an essential role in keeping North Dakota's energy supply dependable and cost-effective.
Public input and transparency
Says that as manager of the PSC's consumer affairs portfolio she has prioritized public input and increased transparency through regular public meetings and constituent outreach.
Infrastructure growth and landowners
Says the biggest challenge facing the PSC is managing rapid growth in energy infrastructure while protecting consumers and landowners.

Background

  • North Dakota Public Service Commissioner, 2022–present (appointed Feb. 11, 2022; elected Nov. 2022)
  • PSC portfolio includes energy regulation, pipeline safety, consumer affairs, cybersecurity and damage prevention
  • Former Human Resources Manager, North Dakota State Tax Commission
  • Former Deputy State Treasurer; also worked in the state securities department
  • More than 30 years in human resources and government administration
  • B.A. in psychology, University of North Dakota; Master of Management, University of Mary
  • Born in Rugby, North Dakota
